g.prompt: She ____ (live) in Basel since 2019.
g.why: Present Perfect mit «since» + Zeitpunkt: Die Handlung begann in der Vergangenheit und dauert bis jetzt an.

g.prompt: I ____ (see) that film last week.
g.why: Mit einer abgeschlossenen Zeitangabe («last week») steht das Past Simple, nicht das Present Perfect.

g.prompt: Look! It ____ (snow).
g.why: «Look!» zeigt, dass etwas gerade jetzt passiert: Present Progressive.

g.prompt: Water ____ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.
g.why: Allgemeingültige Tatsachen stehen im Present Simple; 3. Person Singular mit -s.

g.prompt: When I arrived, the film ____ already ____ (start).
g.why: Die Handlung lag vor einer anderen Handlung in der Vergangenheit: Past Perfect (had + Partizip).

g.prompt: While I ____ (cook), the phone rang.
g.why: Eine länger andauernde Handlung wird durch eine kurze unterbrochen: Past Progressive + Past Simple.

g.prompt: If it ____ (rain) tomorrow, we will stay at home.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 1: im if-Teil Present Simple, im Hauptsatz will.

g.prompt: If I ____ (be) you, I would take the job.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 2: «If I were you» ist die Standardform für Ratschläge; «was» ist umgangssprachlich.

g.prompt: If we had left earlier, we ____ (not miss) the train.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 3: im Hauptsatz would have + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: The new bridge ____ (build) next year.
g.why: Passiv im Futur: will be + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: This castle ____ (build) in the 12th century.
g.why: Passiv Past Simple: was/were + Partizip Perfekt; abgeschlossene Zeitangabe.

g.prompt: I'm looking forward to ____ (see) you.
g.why: Nach «look forward to» folgt das Gerund (-ing), weil «to» hier eine Präposition ist.

g.prompt: She decided ____ (study) medicine.
g.why: Nach «decide» folgt der Infinitiv mit «to».

g.prompt: Would you mind ____ (open) the window?
g.why: Nach «mind» folgt immer das Gerund.

g.prompt: I've been waiting ____ two hours.
g.why: «for» steht vor einer Zeitdauer, «since» vor einem Zeitpunkt.

g.prompt: I've been waiting ____ nine o'clock.
g.why: «since» steht vor einem Zeitpunkt.

g.prompt: The woman ____ lives next door is a doctor.
g.why: Für Personen im notwendigen Relativsatz: who oder that.

g.prompt: That's the man ____ car was stolen.
g.why: «whose» drückt Besitz aus (dessen/deren).

g.prompt: This is the town ____ I grew up.
g.why: Für Orte verwendet man «where» (oder «in which»).

g.prompt: She said that she ____ (be) tired.
g.why: Indirekte Rede mit Einleitung in der Vergangenheit: Present Simple wird zu Past Simple (Backshift).

g.prompt: He told me that he ____ (lose) his keys.
g.why: Indirekte Rede: Past Simple oder Present Perfect wird zu Past Perfect.

g.prompt: She asked me where I ____ (live).
g.why: Indirekte Frage: Aussagesatz-Wortstellung, kein «do», plus Backshift.

g.prompt: My brother is ____ (tall) than me.
g.why: Einsilbige Adjektive: Komparativ mit -er.

g.prompt: This is the ____ (expensive) restaurant in town.
g.why: Mehrsilbige Adjektive: Superlativ mit «the most».

g.prompt: Today is ____ (bad) day of my life!
g.why: «bad» ist unregelmässig: bad – worse – the worst.

g.prompt: She sings very ____ (beautiful).
g.why: Ein Verb wird durch ein Adverb beschrieben (Adjektiv + -ly).

g.prompt: He speaks English very ____ (good).
g.why: Das Adverb zu «good» ist unregelmässig: «well».

g.prompt: You ____ wear a seatbelt. It's the law.
g.why: «must» / «have to» drücken eine Pflicht aus.

g.prompt: You ____ come if you don't want to. It's optional.
g.why: «don't have to» = nicht müssen (keine Pflicht). «mustn't» wäre ein Verbot.

g.prompt: You ____ smoke in the hospital. It's forbidden.
g.why: «mustn't» = nicht dürfen (Verbot).

g.prompt: How ____ money do you have?
g.why: «much» mit unzählbaren Nomen (money).

g.prompt: How ____ friends came to the party?
g.why: «many» mit zählbaren Nomen im Plural.

g.prompt: There aren't ____ apples left.
g.why: In verneinten Sätzen verwendet man «any».

g.prompt: Would you like ____ tea?
g.why: In Angeboten und Bitten steht «some», auch in Fragen.

g.prompt: I've ____ finished my homework.
g.why: «already» = schon (in bejahten Sätzen, zwischen have und Partizip).

g.prompt: Have you finished ____?
g.why: «yet» steht in Fragen und Verneinungen am Satzende.

g.prompt: I ____ (use) to play the piano, but I stopped.
g.why: «used to» beschreibt frühere Gewohnheiten, die es nicht mehr gibt.

g.prompt: Did you ____ (use) to live in Bern?
g.why: In Fragen mit «did» steht die Grundform: «use to».

g.prompt: I'm not used to ____ (get) up so early.
g.why: «be used to» (gewohnt sein) + Gerund.

g.prompt: I wish I ____ (have) more time.
g.why: «wish» für die Gegenwart: wish + Past Simple.

g.prompt: I wish I ____ (not say) that yesterday.
g.why: «wish» für die Vergangenheit: wish + Past Perfect.

g.prompt: It's a nice day, ____ it?
g.why: Question Tag: bejahter Satz → verneinter Tag mit demselben Hilfsverb.

g.prompt: You don't eat meat, ____ you?
g.why: Verneinter Satz → bejahter Tag; Hilfsverb «do».

g.prompt: They went to Paris, ____ they?
g.why: Past Simple ohne Hilfsverb → Tag mit «did».

g.prompt: I had my car ____ (repair) yesterday.
g.why: «have something done»: jemand anderes macht etwas für mich → have + Objekt + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: By the end of the year, I ____ (finish) my apprenticeship.
g.why: Future Perfect: Eine Handlung ist zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Zukunft abgeschlossen.

g.prompt: This time tomorrow, I ____ (lie) on the beach.
g.why: Future Progressive: Handlung, die zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Zukunft gerade abläuft.

g.prompt: Look at the clouds! It ____ (rain).
g.why: «going to» für Vorhersagen mit sichtbaren Anzeichen.

g.prompt: The train ____ (leave) at 6.15 tomorrow morning.
g.why: Fahrpläne und Programme: Present Simple auch für die Zukunft.

g.prompt: I ____ (know) him for ten years.
g.why: «know» ist ein Zustandsverb und steht nicht in der -ing-Form; Present Perfect + for.

g.prompt: Although ____ was raining, we went out.
g.why: Im englischen Satz braucht es immer ein Subjekt: «it was raining».

g.prompt: ____ the rain, we went out.
g.why: «despite» / «in spite of» + Nomen; «although» + Satz.

g.prompt: You won't pass ____ you study.
g.why: «unless» = wenn nicht.

g.prompt: Take an umbrella ____ it rains.
g.why: «in case» = für den Fall, dass (Vorsichtsmassnahme).

g.prompt: She is interested ____ politics.
g.why: Feste Präposition: interested in.

g.prompt: It depends ____ the weather.
g.why: Feste Präposition: depend on (nicht «from»).

g.prompt: I'm afraid ____ spiders.
g.why: Feste Präposition: afraid of.

g.prompt: We arrived ____ London at midnight.
g.why: «arrive in» bei Städten und Ländern, «arrive at» bei Gebäuden/Orten.

g.prompt: My birthday is ____ 5 June.
g.why: «on» vor Daten und Wochentagen.

g.prompt: We usually go skiing ____ February.
g.why: «in» vor Monaten, Jahreszeiten und Jahren.

g.prompt: The meeting is ____ ten o'clock.
g.why: «at» vor Uhrzeiten.

g.prompt: I hurt ____ while I was cooking.
g.why: Reflexivpronomen, wenn Subjekt und Objekt dieselbe Person sind.

g.prompt: This book isn't mine. It's ____ (she).
g.why: Possessivpronomen ohne Nomen: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs.

g.prompt: ____ he nor his sister came to the party.
g.why: «neither … nor» = weder … noch.

g.prompt: There ____ a lot of people at the concert.
g.why: «there were» mit Plural (people).

g.prompt: The news ____ (be) very surprising.
g.why: «news» ist unzählbar und steht mit einem Verb im Singular.

g.prompt: Can you give me some ____? (Rat)
g.why: «advice» ist unzählbar: kein Plural, kein «an».

g.prompt: He's ____ honest man.
g.why: «an» vor Vokal-Laut; das «h» in «honest» ist stumm.

g.prompt: She's ____ university student.
g.why: «a» vor Konsonant-Laut; «university» beginnt mit [ju].

g.prompt: I stopped ____ (smoke) two years ago.
g.why: «stop + -ing» = mit etwas aufhören.

g.prompt: On the way home, I stopped ____ (buy) bread.
g.why: «stop + to» = anhalten, um etwas zu tun.

g.prompt: Remember ____ (lock) the door when you leave.
g.why: «remember + to» = daran denken, etwas (in Zukunft) zu tun.

g.prompt: I remember ____ (meet) her at a party years ago.
g.why: «remember + -ing» = sich an etwas Vergangenes erinnern.

g.prompt: My parents let me ____ (go) to the concert.
g.why: Nach «let» + Objekt steht der Infinitiv ohne «to».

g.prompt: The teacher made us ____ (rewrite) the essay.
g.why: Nach «make» + Objekt steht der Infinitiv ohne «to».

g.prompt: She wants me ____ (help) her.
g.why: want + Objekt + to-Infinitiv (nicht «that»-Satz).

g.prompt: The more you practise, ____ better you get.
g.why: «the + Komparativ …, the + Komparativ» = je … desto.

g.prompt: It was ____ a nice day that we went to the lake.
g.why: «such (a) + Adjektiv + Nomen … that»; «so» nur vor Adjektiv allein.

g.prompt: The film was ____ boring that I fell asleep.
g.why: «so + Adjektiv + that».

g.prompt: ____ have I seen such a mess!
g.why: Inversion nach verneinenden Adverbien am Satzanfang: Never have I …

g.prompt: You ____ have told me! I would have helped you.
g.why: «should have + Partizip» = Vorwurf/Bedauern über etwas Vergangenes.

g.prompt: She isn't answering. She ____ be asleep.
g.why: «must» = logische Schlussfolgerung (sie muss wohl schlafen).

g.prompt: That ____ be true! I saw him five minutes ago.
g.why: «can't» = Unmöglichkeit, logischer Schluss im Negativen.

g.prompt: It's high time you ____ (find) a job.
g.why: «It's (high) time» + Past Simple.

g.prompt: I'd rather you ____ (not tell) anyone.
g.why: «would rather + Person» + Past Simple.

g.prompt: He's been working here ____ he left school.
g.why: «since» kann auch einen Nebensatz einleiten (seit).

g.prompt: The report needs to ____ (finish) by Friday.
g.why: Passiv-Infinitiv: to be + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: My bike ____ (steal)! I can't find it anywhere.
g.why: Passiv im Present Perfect: has been + Partizip; das Resultat ist jetzt wichtig.

g.prompt: The road ____ (repair) at the moment.
g.why: Passiv im Present Progressive: is being + Partizip.

g.prompt: English ____ (speak) in many countries.
g.why: Passiv Present Simple: is/are + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: He is said ____ (be) very rich.
g.why: «be said to» + Infinitiv (unpersönliches Passiv).

g.prompt: Having ____ (finish) the work, she went home.
g.why: Partizipialsatz der Vorzeitigkeit: Having + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: ____ she studied harder, she would pass.
g.why: Der if-Satz Typ 2 beginnt mit «If» + Past Simple; im Hauptsatz steht «would».

g.prompt: What ____ you do if you lost your phone?
g.why: if-Satz Typ 2: im Hauptsatz «would».

g.prompt: She ____ (work) here for five years by next March.
g.why: Future Perfect mit «by» + Zeitpunkt in der Zukunft.

g.prompt: I ____ (not see) her since Christmas.
g.why: Present Perfect mit «since»; Verneinung mit haven't.

g.prompt: How long ____ you ____ (learn) English?
g.why: Present Perfect Progressive für die Dauer einer andauernden Tätigkeit.

g.prompt: By the time we got there, everyone ____ (go) home.
g.why: Past Perfect: vor einem anderen Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit abgeschlossen.

g.prompt: I ____ to London three times.
g.why: «have been to» = schon dort gewesen und zurückgekehrt (Erfahrung). «have gone to» = ist hingegangen und noch dort.

g.prompt: She ____ her leg when she was skiing.
g.why: Kurze Handlung in einer abgeschlossenen Vergangenheitssituation: Past Simple.

g.prompt: We ____ dinner when the lights went out.
g.why: Andauernde Handlung, die unterbrochen wird: Past Progressive.

g.prompt: I ____ English for six years now.
g.why: Dauer bis jetzt mit «for … now»: Present Perfect Progressive; Deutsch «seit» ist hier kein Präsens.

g.prompt: If I ____ rich, I would travel the world.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 2: If + Past Simple («were» für alle Personen möglich).

g.prompt: If you heat ice, it ____.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 0 (allgemeine Wahrheit): Present Simple in beiden Teilen.

g.prompt: If she had asked me, I ____ her.
g.why: if-Satz Typ 3: would have + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: I'll call you when I ____ home.
g.why: Nach «when» mit Zukunftsbezug steht das Present Simple, nicht «will».

g.prompt: The letter ____ yesterday.
g.why: Passiv mit abgeschlossener Zeitangabe: Past Simple Passiv.

g.prompt: A new school ____ in our village at the moment.
g.why: Passiv im Present Progressive: gerade im Gang.

g.prompt: He asked me ____.
g.why: Indirekte Frage: Aussagesatz-Wortstellung und Backshift, kein «did».

g.prompt: She told me ____ late.
g.why: Verneinte Aufforderung in der indirekten Rede: tell sb not to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: The man ____ wallet was stolen went to the police.
g.why: «whose» = dessen (Besitz).

g.prompt: Zermatt, ____ is near the Matterhorn, is very popular.
g.why: Im nicht notwendigen Relativsatz (mit Kommas) darf «that» nicht stehen; für Dinge «which».

g.prompt: ____ I need is a long holiday.
g.why: «What» = das, was (bezieht sich auf nichts Vorangehendes).

g.prompt: I enjoy ____ in the mountains.
g.why: Nach «enjoy» folgt immer das Gerund.

g.prompt: I can't afford ____ a new car.
g.why: Nach «afford» folgt der Infinitiv mit «to».

g.prompt: She's very good ____ languages.
g.why: Feste Präposition: good at.

g.prompt: We're going on holiday ____ Monday.
g.why: «on» vor Wochentagen.

g.prompt: I've lived here ____ 2018.
g.why: «since» + Zeitpunkt.

g.prompt: I moved here three years ____.
g.why: «ago» steht nach der Zeitangabe und mit Past Simple.

g.prompt: There isn't ____ milk in the fridge.
g.why: «much» mit unzählbaren Nomen in verneinten Sätzen.

g.prompt: I have ____ friends in Geneva, so I visit often.
g.why: «a few» = einige (zählbar, positiv). «few» = wenige (negativ).

g.prompt: There is ____ time left – hurry up!
g.why: «little» = wenig (unzählbar, negativ betont).

g.prompt: There are ____ cars in the city centre than before.
g.why: «fewer» mit zählbaren Nomen (cars), «less» mit unzählbaren.

g.prompt: This is ____ book I've ever read.
g.why: Superlativ von «good»: the best; bei «ever» steht oft der Superlativ.

g.prompt: My sister is not as tall ____ me.
g.why: Vergleich der Gleichheit: as … as.

g.prompt: He drives ____ than his father.
g.why: Komparativ des Adverbs «carefully»: more carefully.

g.prompt: She speaks Italian ____.
g.why: Adverb zur Beschreibung des Verbs.

g.prompt: I feel ____ today.
g.why: Nach «feel» (Zustand/Gefühl) steht ein Adjektiv. «well» geht auch im Sinne von gesund, ist hier aber nicht als Option.

g.prompt: You ____ touch that! It's very hot.
g.why: Verbot: mustn't.

g.prompt: We ____ wear a uniform at our school, but we can if we want.
g.why: Keine Pflicht: don't have to.

g.prompt: You look tired. You ____ go to bed earlier.
g.why: Ratschlag: should.

g.prompt: ____ you help me carry these boxes?
g.why: Höfliche Bitte: Could you …?

g.prompt: I ____ swim when I was five.
g.why: Fähigkeit in der Vergangenheit: could.

g.prompt: He ____ have forgotten. He never forgets anything.
g.why: «can't have» = es ist unmöglich, dass er es vergessen hat.

g.prompt: She ____ have missed the bus – she's never late.
g.why: «must have» = sicherer Schluss über die Vergangenheit.

g.prompt: I ____ play football every weekend when I was a kid.
g.why: Frühere Gewohnheit: used to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: I'm not used to ____ on the left.
g.why: be used to + Gerund (gewohnt sein).

g.prompt: I wish I ____ speak Chinese.
g.why: wish + could für unerfüllte Fähigkeiten in der Gegenwart.

g.prompt: If only I ____ to the doctor earlier!
g.why: «If only» für Bedauern über Vergangenes: + Past Perfect.

g.prompt: You're coming tonight, ____?
g.why: Bejahter Satz mit «are» → Tag «aren't you».

g.prompt: She can't swim, ____?
g.why: Verneinter Satz → bejahter Tag mit «can».

g.prompt: Let's go out, ____?
g.why: Nach «Let's» lautet der Tag «shall we».

g.prompt: I'm right, ____?
g.why: Nach «I am» lautet der Tag umgangssprachlich «aren't I».

g.prompt: We got our house ____ last year.
g.why: get/have + Objekt + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: ____ it was cold, we went swimming.
g.why: «Although» + Satz; «Despite» + Nomen.

g.prompt: ____ his injury, he played the whole match.
g.why: «Despite» + Nomen (ohne «of»).

g.prompt: The hotel was expensive. ____, it was very comfortable.
g.why: «However» verbindet zwei Hauptsätze (mit Punkt/Komma).

g.prompt: I'll lend you my bike ____ you bring it back tomorrow.
g.why: «as long as» = solange, unter der Bedingung dass.

g.prompt: She saved money ____ she could buy a car.
g.why: «so that» + Satz drückt den Zweck aus.

g.prompt: I don't know ____ he will come or not.
g.why: «whether … or not» = ob … oder nicht.

g.prompt: ____ of my parents speaks English. They only speak German.
g.why: «Neither of» = keiner von beiden (zwei Personen).

g.prompt: ____ students in the class passed the exam.
g.why: «all (the)» + Plural; «every/each» + Singular.

g.prompt: Could you give me ____ information about the course?
g.why: «information» ist unzählbar: some information.

g.prompt: My ____ is in the car.
g.why: «luggage» ist unzählbar, kein Plural.

g.prompt: She plays ____ piano very well.
g.why: Bei Musikinstrumenten steht normalerweise «the».

g.prompt: ____ life is too short to be unhappy.
g.why: Bei abstrakten Nomen im allgemeinen Sinn steht kein Artikel.

g.prompt: I usually go to school ____ bus.
g.why: Verkehrsmittel: by bus, by train (ohne Artikel).

g.prompt: We met ____ the station.
g.why: Treffpunkt: at the station.

g.prompt: They talked to ____ for hours.
g.why: «each other» = einander (gegenseitig).

g.prompt: Did you enjoy ____ at the party?
g.why: «enjoy oneself» = sich amüsieren (reflexiv).

g.prompt: Is this jacket ____?
g.why: Possessivpronomen ohne Nomen: yours (ohne Apostroph).

g.prompt: I'll be back ____ an hour.
g.why: «in + Zeitraum» = in (Zukunft, nach Ablauf).

g.prompt: Please finish the project ____ Friday at the latest.
g.why: «by» = spätestens bis.

g.prompt: The shop is open ____ 8 p.m.
g.why: «until» = bis (Dauer bis zu einem Zeitpunkt).

g.prompt: I'm thinking ____ changing jobs.
g.why: «think of/about + -ing» = überlegen, etwas zu tun.

g.prompt: We need to ____ a decision soon.
g.why: Kollokation: make a decision.

g.prompt: Could you ____ me a favour?
g.why: Kollokation: do sb a favour.

g.prompt: Have you ____ your homework?
g.why: Kollokation: do homework.

g.prompt: Don't ____ a noise – the baby is sleeping.
g.why: Kollokation: make a noise.

g.prompt: Can you ____ me the way to the station?
g.why: «tell sb sth»; «say» hat kein persönliches Objekt ohne «to».

g.prompt: She ____ that she was tired.
g.why: «say (that)» ohne persönliches Objekt.

g.prompt: Can I ____ your pen for a moment?
g.why: «borrow» = sich (aus)leihen.

g.prompt: My parents ____ me some money for the trip.
g.why: «lend» = jemandem etwas leihen; unregelmässig: lend – lent – lent.

g.prompt: Prices have ____ by five percent.
g.why: «rise» (intransitiv, ohne Objekt): rise – rose – risen.

g.prompt: The company ____ salaries last year.
g.why: «raise» (transitiv, mit Objekt) ist regelmässig.

g.prompt: I ____ to the cinema with my friends last night.
g.why: Abgeschlossene Handlung mit «last night»: Past Simple.

g.prompt: What ____ at 8 o'clock last night?
g.why: Handlung, die zu einem Zeitpunkt in der Vergangenheit andauerte.

g.prompt: Who ____ the window?
g.why: Subjektfrage mit «who»: kein «did», Verb im Past Simple.

g.prompt: What ____ last night?
g.why: Subjektfrage: Verb direkt nach «what», ohne «did».

g.prompt: Never ____ such a beautiful view.
g.why: Inversion nach «Never» am Satzanfang.

g.prompt: Hardly ____ arrived when the phone rang.
g.why: Inversion: Hardly had I + Partizip … when.

g.prompt: It's time we ____ home.
g.why: «It's time» + Past Simple.

g.prompt: I'd rather ____ at home tonight.
g.why: «would rather» + Infinitiv ohne «to» (gleiches Subjekt).

g.prompt: You'd better ____ now or you'll be late.
g.why: «had better» + Infinitiv ohne «to».

g.prompt: ____ the email, she closed her laptop.
g.why: Partizipialsatz der Vorzeitigkeit: Having + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: The girl ____ next to me is my cousin.
g.why: Partizip Präsens als verkürzter Relativsatz (who is sitting).

g.prompt: It was my brother ____ broke the vase.
g.why: Cleft Sentence: It was + Person + who.

g.prompt: The more you read, ____ you learn.
g.why: Je … desto: the + Komparativ, the + Komparativ.

g.prompt: She is ____ a good cook that everyone loves her food.
g.why: «such a + Adjektiv + Nomen … that».

g.prompt: The box is too heavy ____ me to carry.
g.why: too + Adjektiv + for + Person + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Are you old ____ to vote?
g.why: Adjektiv + enough + to.

g.prompt: The film ____ at 8 p.m., so don't be late.
g.why: Programmzeiten: Present Simple.

g.prompt: I think it ____ rain later.
g.why: Vorhersage ohne klares Anzeichen mit «I think»: will.

g.prompt: Wait, I ____ help you with that bag.
g.why: Spontaner Entschluss/Angebot: will.

g.prompt: We ____ our grandparents next Sunday – it's all arranged.
g.why: Fest vereinbarter Termin: Present Progressive.

g.prompt: By 2030, scientists ____ a cure for this disease.
g.why: Future Perfect: «by» + Zeitpunkt in der Zukunft.

g.prompt: He ____ to be the best player in the team.
g.why: Unpersönliches Passiv: be said to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: The results ____ next week.
g.why: Passiv im Futur.

g.prompt: Mobile phones ____ be switched off during the exam.
g.why: Passiv mit Modalverb: must be + Partizip.

g.prompt: She avoided ____ the question.
g.why: Nach «avoid» folgt das Gerund.

g.prompt: He refused ____ the documents.
g.why: Nach «refuse» folgt der Infinitiv mit «to».

g.prompt: I'm sorry, I didn't mean ____ you.
g.why: «mean to» = beabsichtigen.

g.prompt: Try ____ the computer off and on again.
g.why: «try + -ing» = etwas ausprobieren (als Experiment).

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «Someone stole my bike.»
accept: My bike was stolen by someone.
g.why: Passiv Past Simple: Objekt wird Subjekt, was/were + Partizip. «by someone» lässt man meist weg.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «They speak French in Geneva.»
g.why: Passiv Present Simple: is/are + Partizip Perfekt; «they» (man) fällt weg.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «The company will open a new shop.»
g.answer: A new shop will be opened by the company.
accept: A new shop will be opened by the company.
A new shop will be opened.
g.why: Passiv Futur: will be + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «They have cancelled the concert.»
accept: The concert has been cancelled by them.
g.why: Passiv Present Perfect: has/have been + Partizip.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «They are building a new stadium.»
g.answer: A new stadium is being built.
accept: A new stadium is being built.
g.why: Passiv Present Progressive: is/are being + Partizip.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «You must switch off your phones.»
g.answer: Your phones must be switched off.
accept: Your phones must be switched off.
g.why: Passiv mit Modalverb: Modalverb + be + Partizip.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.»
g.answer: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
accept: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.
g.why: Wenn der Handelnde wichtig ist, nennt man ihn mit «by».

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «People say that he is a genius.» (Beginne mit «He …»)
g.answer: He is said to be a genius.
accept: He is said to be a genius.
g.why: Unpersönliches Passiv: Subjekt + is said + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «Somebody had already repaired the car.»
g.answer: The car had already been repaired.
accept: The car had already been repaired.
g.why: Passiv Past Perfect: had been + Partizip.

g.prompt: Setze ins Passiv: «They gave me a present.» (Beginne mit «I …»)
g.why: Bei zwei Objekten wird oft die Person zum Subjekt: I was given …

g.prompt: Setze ins Aktiv: «The letter was written by my grandmother.»
g.why: Aktiv: Der Handelnde (by …) wird Subjekt, Past Simple.

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: She said, «I am tired.»
accept: She said that she was tired.
g.why: Backshift: Present Simple → Past Simple; Pronomen anpassen.

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: He said, «I will call you tomorrow.»
g.answer: He said he would call me the next day.
accept: He said he would call me the next day.
He said that he would call me the following day.
He said he would call me the following day.
He said that he would call me the next day.
g.why: will → would; tomorrow → the next/following day.

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: She said, «I have lost my keys.»
g.answer: She said she had lost her keys.
accept: She said she had lost her keys.
She said that she had lost her keys.
g.why: Present Perfect → Past Perfect; my → her.

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: Tom said, «I bought a new car.»
g.answer: Tom said he had bought a new car.
accept: Tom said he had bought a new car.
Tom said that he had bought a new car.
Tom said he bought a new car.
g.why: Past Simple → Past Perfect (in der Umgangssprache bleibt oft Past Simple).

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: The teacher said to us, «Close your books.»
g.answer: The teacher told us to close our books.
accept: The teacher told us to close our books.
g.why: Aufforderung: tell + Objekt + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Indirekte Rede: My mum said to me, «Don't be late.»
g.answer: My mum told me not to be late.
accept: My mum told me not to be late.
g.why: Verneinte Aufforderung: tell + Objekt + not to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Indirekte Frage: She asked me, «Where do you live?»
g.answer: She asked me where I lived.
accept: She asked me where I lived.
g.why: Indirekte Frage: Aussagesatz-Wortstellung, kein «do», Backshift.

g.prompt: Indirekte Frage: He asked, «Are you hungry?»
g.answer: He asked if I was hungry.
accept: He asked if I was hungry.
He asked whether I was hungry.
He asked me if I was hungry.
He asked me whether I was hungry.
g.why: Ja/Nein-Fragen: if/whether + Aussagesatz.

g.prompt: Indirekte Frage: She asked, «What time does the train leave?»
g.answer: She asked what time the train left.
accept: She asked what time the train left.
She asked me what time the train left.
g.why: Indirekte Frage: kein «does», Verb im Past Simple.

g.prompt: Höfliche indirekte Frage: «Where is the station?» (Beginne mit «Could you tell me …»)
g.answer: Could you tell me where the station is?
accept: Could you tell me where the station is?
g.why: Nach «Could you tell me» folgt die Aussagesatz-Wortstellung: where the station is.

g.prompt: Höfliche indirekte Frage: «When does the shop open?» (Beginne mit «Do you know …»)
g.answer: Do you know when the shop opens?
accept: Do you know when the shop opens?
g.why: Kein «does» im indirekten Fragesatz; 3. Person -s.

g.prompt: Verbinde mit einem Relativpronomen: «I have a friend. She lives in Paris.»
g.answer: I have a friend who lives in Paris.
accept: I have a friend who lives in Paris.
I have a friend that lives in Paris.
g.why: Für Personen: who/that.

g.prompt: Verbinde mit einem Relativpronomen: «This is the book. I told you about it.»
g.answer: This is the book I told you about.
accept: This is the book that I told you about.
This is the book which I told you about.
This is the book I told you about.
This is the book about which I told you.
g.why: Das Relativpronomen kann wegfallen, wenn es Objekt ist; die Präposition steht meist am Ende.

g.prompt: Verbinde mit «whose»: «That's the girl. Her father is a pilot.»
g.answer: That's the girl whose father is a pilot.
accept: That's the girl whose father is a pilot.
That is the girl whose father is a pilot.
g.why: «whose» ersetzt den Possessivbegleiter (her).

g.prompt: Verbinde mit «where»: «This is the café. We first met there.»
g.answer: This is the café where we first met.
accept: This is the café where we first met.
This is the café in which we first met.
g.why: «where» ersetzt eine Ortsangabe (there).

g.prompt: Verbinde mit «which» (nicht notwendiger Relativsatz): «Bern is the capital. It has a beautiful old town.»
g.answer: Bern, which is the capital, has a beautiful old town.
accept: Bern, which is the capital, has a beautiful old town.
Bern, which has a beautiful old town, is the capital.
g.why: Zusatzinformation zwischen Kommas, nur «which» (nicht «that»).

g.prompt: Schreibe einen if-Satz Typ 1: «Study hard. You'll pass.» (Beginne mit «If …»)
g.answer: If you study hard, you'll pass.
accept: If you study hard, you'll pass.
If you study hard, you will pass.
g.why: Typ 1: If + Present Simple, will + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe einen if-Satz Typ 2: «I don't have a car, so I can't drive to work.»
g.answer: If I had a car, I could drive to work.
accept: If I had a car, I could drive to work.
If I had a car, I would drive to work.
If I had a car I could drive to work.
g.why: Typ 2 für irreale Gegenwart: If + Past Simple, would/could + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe einen if-Satz Typ 3: «I didn't know you were ill, so I didn't visit you.»
g.answer: If I had known you were ill, I would have visited you.
accept: If I had known you were ill, I would have visited you.
If I'd known you were ill, I would have visited you.
If I had known you were ill, I'd have visited you.
If I'd known you were ill, I'd have visited you.
g.why: Typ 3 für irreale Vergangenheit: If + Past Perfect, would have + Partizip.

g.prompt: Schreibe einen if-Satz Typ 3: «We missed the bus because we left late.»
g.answer: If we hadn't left late, we wouldn't have missed the bus.
accept: If we hadn't left late, we wouldn't have missed the bus.
If we had not left late, we would not have missed the bus.
We wouldn't have missed the bus if we hadn't left late.
g.why: Die Verneinung kehrt sich im irrealen Satz um.

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «unless»: «If you don't hurry, you'll miss the train.»
g.answer: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train.
accept: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.
You'll miss the train unless you hurry.
g.why: «unless» = if … not; das Verb im unless-Teil ist bejaht.

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «I wish»: «I'm not tall.»
g.why: wish + Past Simple für die Gegenwart («were» ist formeller).

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «I wish»: «I didn't study for the test.»
g.answer: I wish I had studied for the test.
accept: I wish I had studied for the test.
I wish I'd studied for the test.
g.why: wish + Past Perfect für Bedauern über die Vergangenheit.

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «I wish»: «I can't speak Spanish.»
g.answer: I wish I could speak Spanish.
accept: I wish I could speak Spanish.
g.why: wish + could für fehlende Fähigkeiten.

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «used to»: «When I was a child, I played with dolls. Now I don't.»
g.answer: I used to play with dolls.
accept: I used to play with dolls.
When I was a child, I used to play with dolls.
g.why: «used to» für frühere Gewohnheiten.

g.prompt: Schreibe mit «didn't use to»: «I didn't like vegetables when I was young, but now I do.»
g.answer: I didn't use to like vegetables.
accept: I didn't use to like vegetables.
I didn't use to like vegetables when I was young.
g.why: Verneinung: didn't use to (ohne -d).

g.prompt: Bilde eine Frage zum unterstrichenen Teil: «She lives in Bern.» (in Bern)
g.why: W-Frage im Present Simple: Fragewort + does + Subjekt + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Bilde eine Frage: «They went to Italy last summer.» (Wohin?)
g.answer: Where did they go last summer?
accept: Where did they go last summer?
g.why: Past Simple-Frage: did + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Bilde eine Subjektfrage: «Anna broke the window.» (Wer?)
g.why: Fragt man nach dem Subjekt, steht kein «did».

g.prompt: Bilde eine Frage: «He has been waiting for an hour.» (Wie lange?)
g.answer: How long has he been waiting?
accept: How long has he been waiting?
g.why: Present Perfect Progressive-Frage: How long + has + Subjekt + been + -ing.

g.prompt: Verneine: «She has finished her homework.»
accept: She has not finished her homework.
She hasn't finished her homework yet.
g.why: Present Perfect: has not / hasn't + Partizip.

g.prompt: Verneine: «I went to the party.»
g.answer: I didn't go to the party.
accept: I didn't go to the party.
I did not go to the party.
g.why: Past Simple: didn't + Infinitiv (nicht «didn't went»).

g.prompt: Verneine: «He likes coffee.»
g.why: Present Simple 3. Person: doesn't + Infinitiv ohne -s.

g.prompt: Bilde den Komparativ: «My bag is heavy. Your bag is heavier.» Schreibe einen Satz mit «not as … as».
g.answer: My bag is not as heavy as your bag.
accept: My bag is not as heavy as your bag.
My bag isn't as heavy as your bag.
My bag isn't as heavy as yours.
My bag is not as heavy as yours.
g.why: not as + Grundform + as.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «the … the»: «If you train more, you get fitter.»
g.answer: The more you train, the fitter you get.
accept: The more you train, the fitter you get.
g.why: Je … desto: The + Komparativ, the + Komparativ.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «too»: «The coffee is very hot. I can't drink it.»
g.answer: The coffee is too hot to drink.
accept: The coffee is too hot to drink.
The coffee is too hot for me to drink.
g.why: too + Adjektiv + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «enough»: «He is very young. He can't vote.»
g.answer: He isn't old enough to vote.
accept: He isn't old enough to vote.
He is not old enough to vote.
g.why: not + Adjektiv + enough + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «so … that»: «It was very cold. The lake froze.»
g.answer: It was so cold that the lake froze.
accept: It was so cold that the lake froze.
It was so cold the lake froze.
g.why: so + Adjektiv + that + Folge.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «such … that»: «It was a very good film. We watched it twice.»
g.answer: It was such a good film that we watched it twice.
accept: It was such a good film that we watched it twice.
g.why: such + a + Adjektiv + Nomen + that.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «although»: «It rained. We went for a walk.»
g.answer: Although it rained, we went for a walk.
accept: Although it rained, we went for a walk.
We went for a walk although it rained.
Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
g.why: «although» + vollständiger Satz.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «despite»: «Although it rained, we went for a walk.»
g.answer: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
accept: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
We went for a walk despite the rain.
g.why: «despite» + Nomen (hier: the rain).

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «in spite of» + -ing: «Although she was tired, she kept working.»
g.answer: In spite of being tired, she kept working.
accept: In spite of being tired, she kept working.
She kept working in spite of being tired.
Despite being tired, she kept working.
g.why: in spite of / despite + Gerund.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «so that»: «I wrote it down. I didn't want to forget it.»
g.answer: I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget it.
accept: I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget it.
I wrote it down so I wouldn't forget it.
g.why: «so that» + would/could für den Zweck in der Vergangenheit.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «in order to»: «She works hard because she wants to save money.»
g.answer: She works hard in order to save money.
accept: She works hard in order to save money.
g.why: «in order to» + Infinitiv für den Zweck.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «neither … nor»: «My brother doesn't smoke. My sister doesn't smoke.»
g.answer: Neither my brother nor my sister smokes.
accept: Neither my brother nor my sister smokes.
Neither my brother nor my sister smoke.
g.why: «neither … nor» = weder … noch; Verb nach dem näheren Subjekt im Singular.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «both … and»: «Tom plays tennis. Lisa plays tennis too.»
g.answer: Both Tom and Lisa play tennis.
accept: Both Tom and Lisa play tennis.
g.why: «both … and» + Verb im Plural.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit Gerund als Subjekt: «It is fun to swim in the lake.»
g.answer: Swimming in the lake is fun.
accept: Swimming in the lake is fun.
g.why: Gerund als Subjekt am Satzanfang.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «have something done»: «A hairdresser cut my hair yesterday.»
g.answer: I had my hair cut yesterday.
accept: I had my hair cut yesterday.
I got my hair cut yesterday.
g.why: have/get + Objekt + Partizip Perfekt.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «have something done»: «A mechanic is repairing our car.»
g.answer: We are having our car repaired.
accept: We are having our car repaired.
We are getting our car repaired.
g.why: Present Progressive von have + Objekt + Partizip.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit Inversion: «I have never seen such a mess.» (Beginne mit «Never …»)
g.answer: Never have I seen such a mess.
accept: Never have I seen such a mess.
g.why: Nach «Never» am Anfang: Hilfsverb vor Subjekt.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit Inversion: «If I had known, I would have come.» (Beginne mit «Had …»)
g.answer: Had I known, I would have come.
accept: Had I known, I would have come.
Had I known, I'd have come.
g.why: Formelle Inversion im if-Satz Typ 3: Had + Subjekt + Partizip, ohne «if».

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «It was … who»: «My sister found the keys.» (Betone «my sister».)
g.answer: It was my sister who found the keys.
accept: It was my sister who found the keys.
It was my sister that found the keys.
g.why: Cleft Sentence zur Betonung: It was + Element + who/that.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «What …»: «I need a holiday.»
g.answer: What I need is a holiday.
accept: What I need is a holiday.
g.why: Cleft Sentence: What + Subjekt + Verb + is …

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit einem Partizipialsatz: «After she had finished work, she went home.»
g.answer: Having finished work, she went home.
accept: Having finished work, she went home.
g.why: Having + Partizip Perfekt für Vorzeitigkeit; gleiches Subjekt.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit einem Partizip: «The man who is standing at the door is my uncle.»
g.answer: The man standing at the door is my uncle.
accept: The man standing at the door is my uncle.
g.why: Verkürzter Relativsatz mit Partizip Präsens (-ing).

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «must have»: «I'm sure he forgot.»
g.why: must have + Partizip = sichere Vermutung über die Vergangenheit.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «can't have»: «I'm sure she didn't steal it.»
g.why: can't have + Partizip = es ist unmöglich, dass …

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «should have»: «It was a mistake not to tell her.» (Beginne mit «I …»)
g.why: should have + Partizip = Bedauern/Kritik.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «might»: «Perhaps she will come later.»
g.why: might/may = vielleicht (Möglichkeit).

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «don't have to»: «It isn't necessary for you to come.»
accept: You do not have to come.
g.why: don't have to = nicht müssen.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «mustn't»: «It is forbidden to park here.» (Beginne mit «You …»)
g.why: mustn't = Verbot.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «be able to» im Futur: «I can't come tomorrow.»
g.answer: I won't be able to come tomorrow.
accept: I won't be able to come tomorrow.
I will not be able to come tomorrow.
g.why: «can» hat kein Futur; man verwendet will be able to.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu im Present Perfect mit «for»: «I started living here five years ago.»
g.answer: I have lived here for five years.
accept: I have lived here for five years.
I've lived here for five years.
I have been living here for five years.
I've been living here for five years.
g.why: Present Perfect + for + Dauer, wenn die Handlung noch andauert.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu im Present Perfect mit «since»: «I last saw him in 2020.» (Beginne mit «I haven't …»)
accept: I have not seen him since 2020.
g.why: Verneintes Present Perfect + since.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «It's … since»: «I haven't been to the cinema for months.»
g.answer: It's months since I last went to the cinema.
accept: It's months since I last went to the cinema.
It's been months since I last went to the cinema.
It is months since I last went to the cinema.
It's months since I went to the cinema.
It's been months since I went to the cinema.
g.why: It's/It's been + Zeitraum + since + Past Simple.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «going to»: «I plan to visit my aunt next week.»
g.answer: I'm going to visit my aunt next week.
accept: I'm going to visit my aunt next week.
I am going to visit my aunt next week.
g.why: «going to» für Absichten und Pläne.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «by the time» und Past Perfect: «The film started. Then we arrived.»
g.answer: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
accept: By the time we arrived, the film had started.
By the time we arrived, the film had already started.
The film had started by the time we arrived.
The film had already started by the time we arrived.
g.why: Die frühere Handlung steht im Past Perfect.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «be used to»: «Living alone is normal for me now.»
accept: I am used to living alone.
I'm used to living alone now.
I am used to living alone now.
g.why: be used to + Gerund = an etwas gewöhnt sein.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «would rather»: «I prefer to stay at home tonight.»
g.answer: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
accept: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
I would rather stay at home tonight.
g.why: would rather + Infinitiv ohne to.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «had better»: «It would be a good idea to leave now.» (Beginne mit «We …»)
g.why: had better + Infinitiv ohne to = sollte besser.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «It's time»: «We should go home now.»
accept: It is time we went home.
It's time for us to go home.
g.why: It's time + Subjekt + Past Simple oder It's time to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «too … for … to»: «The box is very heavy. I can't lift it.»
g.answer: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
accept: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
g.why: too + Adjektiv + for + Person + to + Verb (ohne «it»).

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «look forward to»: «I'm excited that I will see you soon.»
g.answer: I'm looking forward to seeing you soon.
accept: I'm looking forward to seeing you soon.
I am looking forward to seeing you soon.
I look forward to seeing you soon.
g.why: look forward to + Gerund.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «suggest»: «Let's take a break,» she said.
accept: She suggested that we take a break.
She suggested that we should take a break.
She suggested that we took a break.
g.why: suggest + Gerund oder suggest that + Subjekt + (should) + Infinitiv; nicht «suggest to».

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «admit»: «Yes, I broke the window,» he said.
accept: He admitted that he had broken the window.
He admitted having broken the window.
He admitted to breaking the window.
g.why: admit + Gerund oder that-Satz.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «refuse»: «I won't pay,» she said.
g.why: refuse + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «promise»: «I'll be on time,» he said.
g.answer: He promised to be on time.
accept: He promised to be on time.
He promised that he would be on time.
He promised he would be on time.
g.why: promise + to-Infinitiv oder that + would.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «remind»: «Don't forget to buy milk,» Mum said to me.
g.answer: Mum reminded me to buy milk.
accept: Mum reminded me to buy milk.
My mum reminded me to buy milk.
g.why: remind + Person + to-Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «warn»: «Don't touch the oven,» he said to the children.
g.answer: He warned the children not to touch the oven.
accept: He warned the children not to touch the oven.
g.why: warn + Person + not to + Infinitiv.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit einem Question Tag: «You're coming tomorrow.»
accept: You are coming tomorrow, aren't you?
g.why: Bejahter Satz → verneinter Tag mit gleichem Hilfsverb.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit einem Question Tag: «She didn't call.»
accept: She did not call, did she?
g.why: Verneinter Satz → bejahter Tag.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu im Past Progressive + Past Simple: «I was in the shower. Then the doorbell rang.» (Beginne mit «I was having …»)
g.answer: I was having a shower when the doorbell rang.
accept: I was having a shower when the doorbell rang.
g.why: Hintergrundhandlung im Past Progressive, unterbrechende Handlung im Past Simple mit «when».

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit «each other»: «Anna helps Ben, and Ben helps Anna.»
g.answer: Anna and Ben help each other.
accept: Anna and Ben help each other.
Ben and Anna help each other.
Anna and Ben help one another.
g.why: «each other» = einander (gegenseitig), nicht «themselves».

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit Possessivpronomen: «This is my pen, not your pen.»
accept: This pen is mine, not yours.
This is my pen, not yours.
g.why: Possessivpronomen ersetzen Possessivbegleiter + Nomen.

g.prompt: Schreibe neu mit Superlativ: «No other mountain in Switzerland is as high as the Dufourspitze.»
g.answer: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
accept: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
g.why: Superlativ: the + Adjektiv-est + in + Ort.

g.prompt: Setze ins Present Perfect Progressive: «I started waiting at ten. I am still waiting.» (Beginne mit «I have …»)
g.answer: I have been waiting since ten.
accept: I have been waiting since ten.
I have been waiting since ten o'clock.
I've been waiting since ten o'clock.
g.why: Present Perfect Progressive (have been + -ing) mit «since» + Zeitpunkt für eine noch andauernde Tätigkeit.

d.situation_de: Du bestellst in einem Café in London etwas zu trinken und zu essen.

turns.s: Hi there, what can I get you?
turns.de: Hallo, was darf ich Ihnen bringen?

turns.s: Could I have a large cappuccino, please?
turns.de: Könnte ich bitte einen grossen Cappuccino haben?

turns.s: Sure. Anything to eat with that?
turns.de: Sicher. Möchten Sie etwas dazu essen?

turns.s: Yes, I'll have a piece of carrot cake.
turns.de: Ja, ich nehme ein Stück Rüeblitorte.

turns.s: Is that to have here or to take away?
turns.de: Zum Hieressen oder zum Mitnehmen?

turns.s: To have here, please. How much is that?
turns.de: Zum Hieressen, bitte. Wie viel macht das?

turns.s: That's six pounds fifty.
turns.de: Das macht sechs Pfund fünfzig.

questions.prompt: Was bestellt die Kundin zu trinken?
why: Falsch: Sie will einen grossen, keinen kleinen Kaffee.
Falsch: Das Büro wird nicht erwähnt.
Falsch: Der Park wird nicht erwähnt.

d.situation_de: Du suchst in einer englischen Stadt den Bahnhof.

turns.s: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the station?
turns.de: Entschuldigung, könnten Sie mir den Weg zum Bahnhof sagen?

turns.s: Of course. Go straight on until you reach the traffic lights.
turns.de: Natürlich. Gehen Sie geradeaus bis zur Ampel.

turns.s: And then?
turns.de: Und dann?

turns.s: Turn left and walk past the church. The station is on your right.
turns.de: Biegen Sie links ab und gehen Sie an der Kirche vorbei. Der Bahnhof ist rechts.
